entry_points.text: Hexdump load runs random formatting and truncation sweeps and signals failure by status; unload does nothing.
Identifier driver runs full checks on a shared instance and reports passed versus run; exit is empty.
Handover has save generation with preservation and restore validation of identity, size, order and checksum; init checks if enabled first.
Open creates state with sync, cache and subscription; release unsubscribes, evicts, tears down and frees; load creates private and coherent devices with unwind.
Unlocked control validates alignment and overflow, clears counters and dispatches to all read, write, migration, exclusive, snapshot, release, flags and unlocked read ops.
Notifiers filter self events, else record sequence under mutex and purge the span; snapshot path has its own invalidation callback.

exports.text: Indexed array offers locked store, erase and destroy plus caller-locked store and erase; store and erase report the prior entry.
Mirror test exposes file behavior and device memory callbacks for release, fault migration and split via operation tables.

hazards.text: Missing pages fail reads and missing or unwritable entries fail writes, causing fault and retry; eviction skips non-migratable pages and warns on unexpected pages.
Reserved entries are rejected; nonblocking alloc failure keeps out-of-memory and stored errors propagate; hexdump mismatches including zero and boundary sizes count as failure.
One-shot fail flag fails next alloc then clears; fault alloc prefers large then single pages and on terminal failure releases locked pages and clears outputs.
Removal marks removing, prunes free entries under spin lock, then evicts, unmaps, releases private backing and frees, ending empty and cleared.
Unwritable destinations report fault errors and alloc failures report memory pressure; split and fault paths must not leak or use absent backing.
Identifier return polarity is inverted and misuse tests emit expected warnings; restore must validate lengths, alignment, order and checksum and free even on mid-loop failure.

invariants.text: Hexdump self test checks output and length against a local model over random layouts, including truncation fill, remainder preservation and boundary sizes with failure tally.
Bounce count advances only after a copied page and sets resume; cached pages hold identities without references and private pages resolve via backing.
Zone selects private versus coherent migration; large order uses folios and small uses single pages, with failed large spans degraded to single pages.
Base plus count ranges reject wrap, need a referenced space and readable containing area, with chunks clamped to request and area ends.
Exclusivity uses a tag denied on scan; snapshots use a temporary notifier with bounded retries and translate only after stable sequence under mutex.

Mapping backs slots with fresh zeroed pages; release frees distinct backing by order and returns pages to pools unless removing; faults align to folio size and split derives tail by offset with missing-backing handling.
Allocator checks need dense allocation from zero, reuse of freed lows, emptiness after destroy, dense bitmap runs, exhaustion past limit and stable size transitions.
Misuse checks tolerate freeing never-allocated values with warnings and honor empty versus populated search; diagnostics rely on generic traces via empty dump.
Preservation stores address plus order with count, checksum and identity; restore rejects magic, compat, size, order or checksum mismatch; generation fills random orders to a ceiling.
User header is idempotent via one inclusion guard and test logging prefixes messages with the module name.

locks.text: Array ops hold the array lock; allocation retry drops then reacquires the same interrupt, bottom-half or process flavor before retry.
Table capacity and slots use a mutex; free lists and count use a spin guard held only around list updates, released before sleeping allocation, with removal holding table stable.
Mirror mutex serializes inserts, bulk maps and verification reads against invalidation; invalidation blocks when allowed else tries nonblocking with no change on contention.
Address space is read-locked during migration setup, exclusive acquisition and faulting, released before user copy or long retries.

state_machines.text: Read and write alternate cached copy under lock with fault fill on missing or unwritable entries until done or fault failure, then finalize count.
Range population retries on busy and sequence-detected invalidation, bounded by time budget when locked and caller timeout when unlocked.
Provisioning reserves backing by zone, grows table when full, maps and publishes before announcing; lifecycle goes from numbering to live exposure with unwind and ordered teardown.
Migration moves in bounded chunks via setup, alloc-copy with large-first then single fallback, install, map and finalize, ending with locked verification readback.
Preservation allocates folio, preserves data, formats metadata and inserts tree, unwinding only completed stages so nothing leaks.
Identifier suite runs emptiness, alloc, destroy, leaf, limit, conversion, misuse and search in order, tallying runs and passes with a final summary.

structs.text: Mirror holds device, flags, mutex, indexed table and notifier; bounce tracks completed count with start, length and buffer for resume.
Device holds chunk table, free page and folio lists, locks and count; chunks pair descriptors with owner and removal mark, intervals pair notifier with mirror.
User command holds five 64-bit slots for address, pointer, requested count, completed count and fault tally for every operation.
Handover state holds folio collection, physical descriptions, preserved tally, descriptive folio and checksum in one static instance.
Harness has four devices, 256 MiB chunks grown by sixteen, fault timeout one thousand, and odd tags one and three for atomic and write.
Controls share one magic with ten sequential numbers for read, write, migrations, exclusive, check, snapshot, release, flags and unlocked read, plus a low-bit fail flag.

Protection byte marks error, none, read, write, two huge sizes, zero, local and remote private and coherent; memory types use zero, private one, coherent two; migration flags mark compound, write, request, valid and ownership.
Handover identity uses four-byte magic for K H O plus exclamation, subtree name and compatibility string.
